 Evaluating the good, bad of Sharks rookie Ivar Stenberg through 12 NHL games 
 Evaluating the good and the bad of San Jose Sharks 19-year-old rookie winger Ivar Stenberg through 12 NHL games. 
 Published 5 hours ago • 
 Updated 5 hours ago 
 BOOKMARKER 
 Share 
 NBC Universal, Inc. 
 Sharks coach Ryan Warsofsky and his players speak with the media after San Jose’s 6-4 loss to the Boston Bruins on Saturday at TD Garden. 
 Editor's note: Sheng Peng is a regular contributor to NBC Sports California’s Sharks coverage. You can read more of his coverage on San Jose Hockey Now , listen to him on the San Jose Hockey Now Podcast , and follow him on Twitter at @Sheng_Peng . 
 Ivar Stenberg, through 12 games, has been terrific on the power play. He’s still a significant work in progress at 5-on-5.
 There’s nothing wrong with that: The Sharks winger is a 19-year-old rookie battling through his D+1 draft year in the best league in the world.

 It’s something special that Stenberg has even excelled on the power play, where he’s piled up seven of his nine points. Most teens wouldn’t be any good at any facet of the NHL, especially not something as important as top power-play unit duty.
 Per Stathletes, here’s what’s been truly impressive about Stenberg on the PP, and what he’s got to work on at 5-on-5.
 Plays under pressure 
 Here’s why Stenberg might not leave PP1 any time soon.

 To the eye, he’s been cool as a cucumber with the puck, veteran-like with the extra space afforded, up a man.
 “He's so calm and he's so confident with the puck, so it doesn't matter if he's getting pressured hard,” Macklin Celebrini said. “If he has a little bit of time and space, he's always able to make that play.”
 He actually leads the Sharks with 50.91 Plays Under Pressure Per 60 on the power play. By Stathletes’ definition, that’s a “successful pass with control where the passer is pressured”.
 He’s been better than superstar Macklin Celebrini in this regard, so far.
 This is absolutely a meaningful stat: Robert Thomas, Jordan Eberle, Connor McDavid, Lucas Raymond and Dylan Strome were top-five in this category last year.
 It won’t surprise anybody that Celebrini led the Sharks in this category last year.
 Pulling off passes under pressure on the power play is so crucial: Drawing in penalty-killing pressure, then making a pass in the face of that pressure, is literally buying time and space for the rest of the power play to attack.
 It’s the literal formula to power play success, deception,and sleight of hand.
 "HE DOES IT AGAIN!" 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/AuuhxjHiAC 
— San Jose Sharks (@SanJoseSharks) October 21, 2026 
 Notice how Stenberg (41) has the patience to make sure all three Montreal Canadiens penalty killers are moving toward him — he sells the shot just enough — before dishing to what everyone knows is the Sharks’ No. 1 option on the power play, the Celebrini one-timer. That split-second of puck poise helps prevent Kaiden Guhle (21) from getting out to block Celebrini’s shot, more likely to happen if Stenberg delivers the pass to Celebrini too early.
 “Having good players around me, that helps [a lot],” Stenberg said. “When you play with good players, they always give you time and space. So yeah, they make it easy for me.”
 But it also is clear that Stenberg is creating time and space for the Sharks’ best players, too.
 “Not a lot of people can do it,” Celebrini said. “Doesn't matter what your age is. I think it's just the kind of player he is.”
 5-on-5 
 Stenberg, however, is lagging in a number of 5-on-5 ways.
 “We have one more player [on the power play],” Stenberg acknowledged. “It's easier. You have the puck more. You can feel the puck.”
 Center Michael Misa and winger Kiefer Sherwood have been his primary linemates, and per Evolving Hockey, their Expected Goals For % as a line is 32.18.
 This, of course, isn’t all on any one of these players.
 But Stathletes’ micro-stats suggest where Stenberg needs to improve to become an impact 5-on-5 winger.
 First things first, simple enough, he’s got to shoot more.
 He’s got 6.87 Shot Attempts per 60, the lowest among all San Jose Sharks forwards, even noted pass-first Alex Wennberg. Smith leads with 15.24.
 “5-on-5, you don't have the puck that much,” Stenberg said. “More chip and chase the puck a lot. So I feel like, sometimes, when you don't get the puck too much, it's hard to create when you finally get the puck. I think that's the newest thing. In Sweden, you have the puck so much, and here you can go like 2-3 shifts without even touching the puck. So probably that's the hardest thing.”
 He wins 1.72 Puck Battles Per 60, only ahead of Smith. Michael Misa, maybe surprisingly, paces the team at 8.28.
 Stenberg forces just 2.58 Turnovers Per 60, last among forwards. Celebrini leads with 10.59 Per 60.
 These are not surprising areas for a 19-year-old to lag in, and Stenberg will improve in all categories as he matures.
 For what it’s worth, there is one surprising defensive area where Stenberg has succeeded, hopefully a sign of better things to come defensively.
 Stenberg leads all Sharks forwards in Puck Deflections Per 60, just ahead of Celebrini and Wennberg. While Stenberg doesn’t seem as confident yet in his body at 5-on-5, he seems to be in the right places mentally and with his stick in passing lanes.
 “I have a long stick,” Stenberg said. “I think that helps a lot.”
 Sharks coach Ryan Warsofsky was far more effusive in his praise: “Smart hockey player. Reads the game really well. He's got a little Mack in him, as far as understanding what the next play might happen, especially when he doesn't have the puck.”
 There is every reason to believe that Stenberg’s power-play success will translate to 5-on-5, eventually. I mean, he’s just 19.
 It’s a long season, and it looks like it’s going to be a long career for Stenberg.
 What Stenberg is good at just might be NHL-elite. What he’s not good at is almost certain to improve with age and experience.
 “Sometimes, I feel like I'm really good and find space, and sometimes, I feel like I'm a little bit lost,” Stenberg admitted. “I'd rather be really good at 5-on-5 than good on the PP. So yeah, hopefully, it's coming soon.”
